entries.name: OpenID Shared Signals Framework, CAEP and RISC
entries.why: Real-time revocation: disconnecting a service or a compromised agent kills its sessions at once instead of at token expiry.

entries.name: DPoP (RFC 9449), Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) and Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396)
entries.why: Sender-constrained tokens and per-action grants so a leaked token is useless and consent is specific.
entries.tracked_by: STD-7: bind issued tokens with DPoP, require resource indicators, express scopes as RAR

entries.tracked_by: STD-8: give each virtual agent a durable ID and short-lived credentials per task; carry the chain in transaction tokens

entries.name: OAuth 2.1 client for remote MCP servers and service connectors (PKCE, RFC 8414, RFC 8707, CIMD, RFC 7591, RFC 7009)
entries.tracked: 2026-11-14: MCP 2026-07-28 prefers Client ID Metadata Documents; dynamic registration kept as fallback until its removal
entries.why: A person links a service by one consent click and a callback; nobody pastes a token. The Worker discovers the authorization server of any remote MCP server, registers itself (CIMD, else DCR), runs auth-code with PKCE S256, seals the tokens per tenant, refreshes and revokes.
